title: Oregon minimum wage at the Hillsboro plant — THE PROCEED PATH
_why_this_case_exists: Case 001 proves the gate ASKS. Nothing proved it does not ask when it should not.
A gate that only ever asks is as broken as one that never does, and it fails in the
more expensive direction: a product that asks three questions before every answer has
reproduced the intake form it was sold as replacing (WORKSPACE.md §4.4). That failure
cannot be seen from inside a single answer — every question looks justified on its own —
so it has to be tested directly.
This case is chosen from the library's own content, and chosen because the determining
fact is ALREADY ESTABLISHED rather than absent.

input.question: What minimum wage do we have to pay at our Hillsboro plant?
input.company_switches: EMPTY — the switch library is not seeded until 6.2

_the_library_row_this_tests_against.trigger_plain: Covered work in Portland metro, standard, or nonurban area.
_the_library_row_this_tests_against._note: The trigger names exactly one determining fact: WHERE the work is. Oregon's minimum wage is set by geography — Portland metro, standard, and nonurban are three different rates.

expected.assertion: ACCEPTANCE — the response is outcome:'answer', not outcome:'ask'. The gate does not stop.
expected.source: DETERMINATION-GATE.md §7 — the bound on asking too much

expected.assertion: The determining fact — where the work is — is reported as KNOWN, sourced from the profile rather than from the user. It must NOT be asked for: migration 010 guarantees every company has a primary site, and DECISIONS.md §25 says state, county and city come from GEOCODING, not from asking.
expected.checkable: response.gate.resolved.known contains a fact matching /worksite (state|county|city)/ with source 'ai_from_profile'
expected._note: This assertion is why the gate reads `entities`. The first version of the spec did not, and this case is what found it.

expected.assertion: The gate does not ask where the plant is. Asking for an established fact is the persistence failure, and it is the one a user reads as the product not listening.

Employee count is genuinely irrelevant to the minimum wage rate — Oregon sets it by geography, not by headcount. It must not appear as a blocking fact. If the gate raises it at all it belongs in non_blocking_unknowns, never in an ask.
expected.checkable: no ask; and if 'employee' appears in resolved.non_blocking_unknowns that is acceptable
expected.source: the library row's own trigger_plain names location and nothing else
expected._note: companies.employee_count is NULL for all 10 companies since migration 006 converted the text bands rather than inventing numbers (DECISIONS.md §21.1). A gate that treated headcount as blocking would therefore block EVERY answer for EVERY company — which is exactly the runaway this case guards against.

expected.assertion: If the gate does record a non-blocking unknown, the ANSWER path may state it conditionally via conditional_on. This is the field the checklist path deliberately does not have.
expected.checkable: lib/answerSchema.ts AnswerPayload has conditional_on; ChecklistAnswer does not, enforced by _ChecklistMayNotHedge

expected.assertion: No specific dollar rate is asserted without a verification badge. Oregon's rates change every 1 July and 0 of 194 library rows carry a citation_url, a quote or a checked date — so any figure came from model memory.

Unlike case 001, an Oregon agency IS correct for this question — BOLI, jurisdiction_level 'state', jurisdiction_state 'Oregon'. The work is in Oregon. The two cases are deliberately opposite on this axis so that 'no Oregon agency' is not mistaken for a general rule.
expected.source: CLAUDE.md §3.2 — jurisdiction is part of the match key, in both directions

_run_note: No baseline recorded yet. Nulls stay null until one is, so an empty result is never mistaken for a pass.
